trial_court: First Additional District Judge, District Burhanpur in HMA No.30/2011
case_name: Smt. Anjana Singh vs Shyam Singh
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Appellant-wife filed a divorce petition against respondent-husband under Section 28 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court passed a decree of dissolution of marriage between the parties under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Appellant-wife appealed against this judgment.

legal_principles.principle: A respondent who fails to establish allegations against the appellant and is found to have harassed the appellant, cannot claim restitution of conjugal rights.
legal_principles.held: It was held that the respondent claimed for financial aid from the parents of the appellant for separate residence at Indore. He failed to establish the allegation against the appellant that she harassed him with her cruel behavior.
cited_cases: Subodh Gupta Vs. Neetu Gupta, (2017) Chh. 196

legal_principles.principle: A respondent who does not make any effort to live with the appellant, cannot claim divorce on grounds of desertion.
legal_principles.held: We find that the respondent did not make any effort to live with the appellant.
cited_cases: Bipinchandra Jaisinghbai Shah Vs. Prabhavati, AIR 1957 SC 176

outcome.final_order: The final court order set aside the decree of dissolution of marriage passed by the trial court and remanded the matter back to the trial court for fresh consideration.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
